description: Manifests every SDK must refuse. Each case is a manifest's YAML text ('yaml'), read as a manifest file with the path 'path' (the YAML parsed, then checked as a manifest), and the error the Python SDK raises for it ('expect'). The cases are the shipped jeff.safety.spam manifest with one number of its is_spam calibration made non-finite (.nan, .inf, -.inf): JSON has no such number, and a threshold of nan would turn calibration off without a word, since `confidence < nan` is always false while the decision still reads as calibrated. An SDK refuses each with a ManifestError or ContractError naming the field and the value; one that reads YAML as the Python SDK does gives the recorded message. The last cases give the spam manifest an alias of the ID form it may not have (only the adapter's ID without its version part may be one: refused for an ID with no version part, two of them, or only one, and for an alias that is the ID itself or another ID), or the same alias twice, each refused with the recorded ManifestError. The access cases give it an access value the manifest schema refuses (access is "owner" or an object whose only field, accounts, lists one or more account ids, each once, of the accounts_keys schema's pattern); each is refused with a ContractError: an SDK whose schema checker words problems as the Python SDK's does gives the recorded message, and every SDK's message starts with its first line and names /access.
